note: Triennial rural district council election. Voting in Tyrone took place on Wednesday 31 May 1933. The Lislea division was the only contested rural district division in the Strabane union; the rest were filled at the nominations (Strabane Chronicle, 22 April 1933, p. 1: 23 members declared elected; no nominations for Birnaghs, Camus, Clady and Killyclooney, whose retiring members were deemed elected). Birnaghs, Camus and Killyclooney are recorded from the 1930 return with the new council's first meetings (every member of the old board returned; each sits in June 1933). Clady is not recorded: its retiring member, Mr. Joseph Mills, wrote declining the councillorship ('When I didn't fill in any paper it was proof that I am done with them'), and the Council declared a vacancy on 13 June 1933 (Strabane Chronicle, 17 June 1933, p. 1); in November 1933 it appointed Mr. Thos. Stewart to fill the vacancy (Strabane Chronicle, 18 November 1933, p. 1), a co-option, not an election. Filed on 1933-05-31, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Tyrone that year (confirmed). division inferred from the 4 June 1930 return (R. J. Buchanan); the Strabane Chronicle, 10 June 1933, p. 8 names the member as returned (every member of the old board returned), and he sits at the new council's first meetings. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
